speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for two months; can you tell me if this pain occurs primarily at rest or if it is triggered by activity like walking or climbing stairs?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Juvenile Arthritis (JIA). The patient's age (24, though symptoms began earlier given the 2-month duration and severity), monoarticular presentation, night pain awakening him from sleep, and failure of NSAIDs are classic for an inflammatory etiology rather than mechanical or infectious causes. Given the severity and duration, I recommend immediate MRI of the left knee to assess for synovitis and bone involvement. REQUEST IMAGES: Left_Knee_MRI. REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid_Factor, ANA.
